results.name: LOTR: Rings of Power Scores High With Critics, But Audiences Aren't Loving It
results.content:
Amazon Studios' *The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power* has finally been released, with critics and fans unable to agree on how to rate the opening two episodes.  
The latest adaptation of the works of J.R.R. Tolkien debuted on the streaming service simultaneously worldwide on Sept. 1 and 2, with the first two episodes able to watch immediately. The feedback on review aggregator [Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_lord_of_the_rings_the_rings_of_power/s01/reviews?type=user) has been decidedly divided, with critics rating the show a respectable 83% while the audience score sits at a comparatively low 37%. Equally, the audience scores are primarily divided between two groups rating the show at either five stars or half a star.  
As far as the critics were concerned, *Rings of Power* deserved praise for its enormous sense of scale and high drama, with [CBR's own Sam Stone](https://www.cbr.com/lotr-rings-of-power-episodes-1-2-review/) saying, "\[the show's] variety of characters and their respective journeys is what keeps *The Rings of Power* engaging and fresh, even in its inevitable slower moments as it sets the stage for its epic tale."
*The Rings of Power* is set in the Second Age of Middle-earth and follows the events leading up to the forging of the titular rings and the rise of the most devout servant of Morgoth, Sauron. Despite its setting thousands of years before the events of *The Hobbit* and *The Lord of the Rings*, the long lives of Elves allowed the show to feature familiar characters like Elrond (Robert Aramayo) and [Galadriel (Morfydd Clark)](https://www.cbr.com/lord-rings-galadriel-cursed-rings-power/).  
Vocal concerns over the original nature of the show led showrunners [Patrick McKay and J. D. Payne to insist](https://www.cbr.com/lotr-the-rings-of-power-insist-firmly-connected-tolkiens-books/) that the show is firmly rooted in the author's original writings. McKay said of the series, "I just want to sort of quibble with the 'vaguely connected' \[wording]. We don't feel that way. We feel like deep roots of this show are in the books and in Tolkien. And if we didn't feel that way, we'd all be terrified to sit up here." This was a view seemingly echoed by the Tolkien Estate, who also responded by saying the show will "bring to the screen previously unexplored stories based on J.R.R. Tolkien's original writings."  
With the series' first two episodes now out in the wild, a further six will be released weekly until all eight are live on Amazon Prime's streaming service.  
Source: [Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_lord_of_the_rings_the_rings_of_power/s01/reviews?type=user)

results.name: The Rings Of Power Season 2's Rotten Tomatoes Score Tops Season 1 In A Major Way - SlashFilm
results.content:
Prime Video's The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has seen a meaningful jump in its Rotten Tomatoes score from season 1 to season 2.
Case in point: Prime Video's "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power." Season 1 of that serialized Middle-earth blockbuster rolled out to decidedly mixed feelings from both the diehard and fair-weather elements of Tolkien fandom. Those opposed were so intense in their reactions that Amazon delayed reviews on its own streaming platform to combat trolls. In the end, Rotten Tomatoes reflected the polarization: Critics gave it an 83% Certified Fresh rating while the audience-driven Popcornmeter inverted the number, sitting at a messy 38%.
The Rings Of Power Season 2's Rotten Tomatoes Score Tops Season 1 In A Major Way
While audience scores are subject to unfair review-bombing from polarized TV viewers, the fact that essentially the same set of critics are back two years later to give this thing such a high rating shows showrunners JD Payne and Patrick McKay have managed to up the ante between seasons.
Other critics point out that as the story progresses, the narrative manages to delve deeper into some of its bigger themes while also giving some of the characters more breathing room to develop and allow the audience to emotionally invest themselves.

results.name: The Rings of Power Officially Reveals First Look at Sauron & Confirms Season 3 Release Date
results.content:
Amazon's ambitious journey into Middle-earth has been a closely watched project for four years. *The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power* carries enormous expectations: its staggering budget, connection to J. R. R. Tolkien's sprawling universe, and expansion beyond Peter Jackson's iconic film trilogy made *Lord of the Rings* fans equal parts nervous and excited. Since its debut in 2022, *The Rings of Power* has sparked massive online debate, but the show remains one of Amazon Prime Video's biggest productions.  
Now, excitement has surged again after the official *Rings of Power* X account shared major news regarding Season 3: an official release date and a first look at Sauron in the show's third installment. With such positive reception during Season 2 of *Rings of Power, Lord of the Rings* fans have a lot to be excited for and more episodes coming later this year.
## The Rings of Power Announces a Release Date & Reveals a First Look  
According to the official *The Rings of Power* X account, Season 3 of the hit fantasy show will release on November 11, 2026 and reveals a first look at Sauron in his signature crown helmet. In the third season, the story will skip ahead several years and place fans right in the midst of the [war between the Elves](https://gamerant.com/lord-of-the-rings-lotr-most-important-elves-lore/) and Sauron, as the Dark Lord attempts to create the One Ring to conquer Middle-earth. It's set to be a much more politically intense and war-driven chapter of the story.  
This announcement seemingly confirms Amazon's commitment to its long-term five-season vision, despite years of debate over ratings, budget concerns, and fan reception. Where Seasons 1 and 2 largely focused on world-building, character introductions, and Sauron's manipulation across Middle-earth, Season 3 will begin transitioning into events that Tolkien fans have been eagerly awaiting, as the next season will likely move into a more direct, consequential stage of the narrative. [The forging of the One Ring](https://gamerant.com/lotr-how-one-ring-creation-explained/) is arguably the most important event of the Second Age, and its arrival raises the stakes dramatically for characters like Galadriel, Elrond, Durin, and Sauron.
## The Rings of Power Didn't Make the Best First Impression Amongst Lord of the Rings Fans  
*The Rings of Power* Season 1 suffered from unfair review bombing after it premiered, where numerous fans expressed their concern with the story's pacing, casting, and accuracy to Tolkien's narrative. However, by the time Season 2 aired, viewers' responses were vastly different. Season 1 received a 38% Rotten Tomatoes audience rating, whereas Season 2 earned a more respectable 58% rating from Rotten Tomatoes audience members. [Charlie Vickers' performance as Sauron](https://gamerant.com/lotr-rings-of-power-saurons-disguises-throughout-middle-earths-history/) was widely praised, and viewers noted the improvement in character dynamics.  
Season 3 is set to improve on its sophomore season even more, with a darker story, far more action, and epic conflict that fans have been waiting for. *The Rings of Power* may never have the same cultural impact as [Peter Jackson's movie trilogy](https://gamerant.com/peter-jackson-lord-of-the-rings-favorite-scene/), but if Season 3 can successfully deliver the epic conflict and emotional intensity of *The Lord of the Rings*, Amazon may finally achieve the version of *The Rings of Power* that fans have been waiting to see since the beginning.

results.name: Why Amazon's $1 Billion "Lord of the Ring" 'Rings of Power' is Losing the Ratings - TechTV Network
results.content:
# Why Amazon’s $1 Billion “Lord of the Ring” ‘Rings of Power’ is Losing the Ratings  
Amazon’s “Lord of the Rings” spinoff, “The Rings of Power,” launched on Prime Video September 1. The company has reportedly spent nearly $1 billion developing the...  
- Amazon’s “Lord of the Rings” spinoff, “The Rings of Power,” launched on Prime Video September 1.
- The company has reportedly spent nearly $1 billion developing the streaming video series.
- The original Tolkien series has a rabid fan base. Upsetting them could hurt Amazon.  
Amazon’s $1 billion bet on its new “Lord of the Rings” streaming TV series is falling flat with initial audiences, posing risks for Amazon Studios and the company’s Prime membership program.  
Though critics have praised the series’ scope and ambition, “The Ring of Power” has rankled with audiences, who gave the show a [39% rating](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_lord_of_the_rings_the_rings_of_power) on Rotten Tomatoes. (By contrast, Peter Jackson’s early 2000s Lord of the Rings trilogy earned audience scores of between 86-95% on Rotten Tomatoes.) Even on Amazon-owned IMDb, audiences rated “The Rings of Power” an anemic 6.8/10.
HBO’s “House of the Dragon,” released last month, is performing much better. It has an 8.8/10 rating in IMDb and an [84% audience score](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/house_of_the_dragon) on Rotten Tomatoes. For each show’s three-day post-debut window, “House of the Dragon” attracted 51% more viewers than “Rings of Power,” according to Whip Media data [reported by TheWrap](https://www.msn.com/en-us/tv/news/whos-winning-the-rings-of-power-vs-house-of-the-dragon-viewership-war-its-complicated-charts/ar-AA11CtBt). The publication also looked at data from Samba TV, which tracks viewership through connected TVs in the US. That told a similar story: 3.1 million households watched the first two episodes of “Rings of Fire” in the first three days, while 4.8 million watched the HBO premier in the same window.  
Counterintuitively, The Lord of the Rings’ rabid fan base, including those obsessed with J.R.R. Tolkien’s original books, may be to blame for Amazon’s challenges.  
“It will be impossible for Amazon to please the millions of Tolkien fans, despite the enormous budget for the series,” Tom Forte, an analyst for investment firm D.A. Davidson wrote in a recent note titled “Jar Jar Binks Ruined My Adulthood” that drew comparisons between “The Rings of Power” and “Star Wars” fans’ outrage over the 1999 movie “The Phantom Menace.”
“It has to succeed. There’s no option.”  
Amazon has said the release of “The Rings of Power” last week was the company’s “biggest premiere ever.” More than 25 million people watched the series the day it dropped, Amazon said in a press release last week, compared to 10.2 million people who watched HBO’s “Game of Thrones” spinoff, “House of the Dragon.”  
The series’ viewership looks smaller, though, compared to the 200 million Prime members who stream videos and TV shows. That raises questions about how worthwhile the series is for the nearly 88% of Amazon Prime members who didn’t watch the premiere – but who are paying an extra $20 year in part to recoup the huge cost of making the series, as well as an annual $1 billion price tag for the streaming rights to Thursday Night Football.  
Amazon executives will be closely watching what percentage of all Prime Video streams the project represents and how many inactive Prime accounts logged on to watch “The Rings of Power,” Insider previously reported.  
An Amazon spokesperson did not respond to questions about how many Prime subscribers have watched “The Rings of Power” since its release last week.  
Amazon insiders, meanwhile, have said the future of Amazon Studios hinges on “The Rings of Power” being a success.

results.name: Prime Video Suspends 'Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power' Reviews
results.content:
By providing your information, you agree to our [Terms of Use](https://pmc.com/terms-of-use) and our [Privacy Policy](https://pmc.com/privacy-policy). We use vendors that may also process your information to help provide our services. Prime Video is forging a new path for “[The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power](https://www.indiewire.com/t/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power/).”  
The big-budget series debuted its first two episodes September 2, with an Amazon source telling [The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power-amazon-review-bombed-1235211190/) that reviews are being held for 72 hours to weed out trolls — and not of the hulking J.R.R. Tolkien variety, though possibly as witless. (Racists have criticized the series’ diverse casting.) “The Rings of Power” currently has a 34 percent average audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, compared to an 87 percent critics score. As of print, there are zero reviews for the series on Prime Video with users unable to post.  
A representative for Prime Video had not returned IndieWire’s request for comment at publish time.
Recently, Disney+ Marvel series “She-Hulk” was confirmed to be “review bombed” on Rotten Tomatoes with an 88 percent critics score distinctly different than the initial 36 percent audience score. The audience score later rose to 50 percent. Review bombing is birthed after a group collaborates to upload negative reviews for its “perceived cultural or political issues rather than its actual quality,” as THR defined the term.  
Current Rotten Tomatoes reviews range from the racially-blind series being slammed for mirroring “current politics” in a story that was “already written and should not have been sullied” to calling it “boring.” One review reads, “Reflecting world diversity in Middle Earth is an odd goal, albeit good for marketing maybe, but it was clearly more important than making a functional TV series.”  
Co-created by showrunners JD PayneandPatrick McKay and already renewed for five seasons, the cast behind “Rings of Power” anticipated [racist backlash](https://www.indiewire.com/2022/02/lord-of-the-rings-series-diverse-casting-backlash-1234698074/).  
When the studio originally released a photo of its multicultural cast, Amazon was immediately met with vitriolic online trolling, as fans took to social media to slam certain roles based on race and gender.
“Obviously there was going to be push and backlash,” Tolkien scholar Mariana Rios Maldonado told [Vanity Fair](https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/02/amazon-the-rings-of-power-series-first-look?utm_brand=vf&utm_source=twitter&mbid=social_twitter&utm_medium=social&utm_social-type=owned), “but the question is, from whom? Who are these people that feel so threatened or disgusted by the idea that an elf is Black or Latino or Asian?”  
Series executive producer Lindsey Weber added, “It felt only natural to us that an adaptation of Tolkien’s work would reflect what the world actually looks like. Tolkien is for everyone. His stories are about his fictional races doing their best work when they leave the isolation of their own cultures and come together.”  
IMDb, which Amazon also owns, has not suspended audience ratings for “Rings of Power.” Currently, the series stands at a 6.1 average score out of 10.  
IndieWire’s Ben Travers gave the series a [B rating](https://www.indiewire.com/2022/08/lord-of-the-rings-review-amazon-rings-of-power-1234756164/), writing, “‘The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ flutters to life in bursts, offering reason enough to believe, with time to play out its own story and optimize its own strengths, the Prime Video creation could leave its own gleaming mark on J.R.R. Tolkien’s still-expanding universe.”

*The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power* is finally set to debut Season 3 [this November](https://movieweb.com/lord-of-the-rings-rings-of-power-season-3-release-date/), but the fate of the series has been revealed ahead of the show's return. The big-budget fantasy epic has been one of Prime Video's most popular titles since its debut in 2022. Despite a drop-off in viewership, the second season was still a major boost to the show's overall numbers. Now, with a third installment officially on the way, Amazon is wasting no time in getting another batch of episodes in the pipeline.  
According to [The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/rings-of-power-season-4-1236605937/), Prime Video has already begun development on *The Rings of Power* Season 4, with pre-production planned for the fall and principal photography aimed for early 2027. The outlet notes that the new season has not been officially greenlit, but considering the production timeline, the streamer is keen on fulfilling its five-season committent for *The Lord of the Rings* prequel series. With filming set for next year, it can be reasonably expected that *Rings of Power* Season 4 premieres sometime in 2028.
As the fourth season begins development, *The Rings of Power* Season 3 is officially set to premiere on Prime Video on Nov. 11. The new season jumps forward several years after the events of the previous finale, with Sauron (Charlie Vickers) closer than ever before to building the One Ring to rule all of Middle-earth. Set during the peak of the conflict between the Elves and Sauron, *The Rings of Power* inches toward the show's endgame, which is known as the War of the Last Alliance, previewed in the opening moments of *The Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring*.  
*The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power* Season 3 comes off a critically acclaimed second season, but audiences are still mixed towards the fantasy epic. On Rotten Tomatoes, Season 2 garnered mostly fresh critic reviews with an 84% score, while user ratings amounted to a far less impressive number at 48% on the Popcornmeter. *Rings of Power* Season 3 will look to close the gap on that divide by flashing forward several years to focus on the action-packed conflict between Sauron and the factions of Middle-earth. Plus, it should help a new cast member from Netflix's biggest show of all time has joined the fold.
While his role remains undisclosed, it is confirmed that *Stranger Things* star Jamie Campbell Bower is set to feature in *The Rings of Power* Season 3. He is speculated to be playing Celeborn, the long-lost husband of Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) who has not showed up in the series yet. If true, expect him to play [a key role](https://movieweb.com/rings-of-power-season-3-missing-lotr-character-celeborn/) in the upcoming season, as his disappearance is one of the main aspects of Galadriel's motivation in the fight against Sauron. The rest of the new cast includes Eddie Marsan (*Clayface*), Andrew Richardson (*Ponies*), Zubin Varla (*Andor*), and Adam Young (*Masters of the Air)*.

results.name: The Wheel Of Time Season 3 Surpasses Rings Of Power
results.content:
### Summary  
- The Wheel of Time is thriving with an 85% Rotten Tomatoes audience score, while The Rings of Power struggles at 38-56%.
- The Rings of Power faces backlash due to writing limitations and deviations from source material, unlike The Wheel of Time.
- Amazon's adaptation of Tolkien's lore is criticized for not having the rights to explore key historical content of Middle-earth.  
Amazon's two big fantasy series, *Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power* and **The Wheel of Time**, are adaptations of books that both have dedicated, long-standing audiences. Their viewers share many overlapping fictional interests with one another. However, when it comes to topping the charts, *The* [Rings of Power](https://gamerant.com/tag/lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power/) is seriously struggling to maintain a positive rating among its followers.
With these two intellectual properties sharing a common audience, why does *The Rings of Power* suffer commercially, while *The Wheel of Time* continues to succeed? Both programs have shared fairly glowing critical ratings over their seasons, with *The Rings of Power* earning 84% on Rotten Tomatoes for both seasons. However, audiences have continued to diverge from the critical consensus, giving Season 1 38%, with Season 2 minorly improving at 56%. This sits in stark contrast to *Wheel of Time's* latest audience score of 85% on Rotten Tomatoes, a new peak for the series. Although *The Wheel of Time* did see a lower audience rating of 60% in its first season due to its sluggish pacing, reception for it has only continued to improve. Now, the show has also surpassed *The Rings of Power* critically, garnering a lofty height of 94% for its third installment.

results.name: 'The Rings of Power' Season 2 Rotten Tomatoes Scores Show Improvement
results.content:
Is Amazon’s hugely expensive *The [Lord of the Rings](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/t/lord-of-the-rings/)* gamble starting to pay off?  
The second-season critic and audience reviews for the much-debated fantasy drama *The [Rings of Power](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/t/rings-of-power/)* show an early improvement compared to the series’ 2022 debut season.  
On Thursday, the company released the new season’s first three episodes onto Prime Video, giving fans the opportunity to sample a significant chunk of the eight-episode season. The initial Rotten Tomatoes critics score is 92 percent “Fresh,” and the audience score is 69 percent positive.
### Related Stories  
It’s easy to forget that the first season received pretty positive critic reviews and averaged 83 percent, but this season has jumped from that. The 69 percent audience score might seem like the less impressive number, but the first season’s audience score was a disastrous 38 percent, so that score has nearly doubled.  
Obviously, this is very much early days, and the scores can and will shift as more episodes get rolled out, but the consensus among critics who have seen episodes beyond the first three seems to be that the remaining hours are at least as good as the opening salvo. (The show’s IMDb scores show a very stable reaction from season one to season two, with both seasons averaging 7.3 of 10, but the Amazon-owned service was also [accused of deleting negative reviews](https://gagadget.com/en/kino/163185-amazon-has-shut-down-access-to-the-rings-of-power-series-rating-and-imdb-deletes-ratings-due-to-a-lot-of-criticism-a/) last time).  
That said, the positive *Rings* reviews still tend to be mixed rather than raves. *The Hollywood Reporter*’s [own review was negative](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-reviews/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power-review-season-2-1235982663/), and *The Washington Post*’s review headline [summarized](https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/tv/2024/08/29/lord-rings-power-review-season-two/) “*The Rings of Power* improves in its second season but not enough.”
Many are comparing *Rings*, once again, to HBO’s *House of the Dragon*. During the shows’ debut seasons, which partially aired head to head in 2022, the overwhelming consensus was that *Dragon* was the superior show. But the second season of *Dragon* was considered a disappointment by some, and *Rings*‘ showrunners seem to have [made good on their pledge](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/rings-of-power-season-2-better-interview-1235985124/) to take note of what was and wasn’t working from their first round. They improved several aspects with a season that has a quickened momentum and given clearer dramatic stakes to complement its consistently gorgeous visuals (and an excellent score by Bear McCreary). (The *Dragon* season two RT scores — based on the entire season, not just three episodes — were 83 percent critics score and 74 percent audience score.)
